messages:
Anya: ran the 8xA100 1F1B perf job on the 4k seq workload this morning. seeing weird tail latency spikes around microbatch boundaries :eyes:
Sam: saw that too. spikes coincide with KV cache "spill" logs in the trace. looks like some microbatches trigger a full-KV sync and an all-reduce fragment :/
Kevin: can you paste the small trace snippet?
Anya: here, from cuprof dump (trimmed):
```
[time 00:12.312] microbatch 7: kv_cache_write start
[time 00:12.345] allreduce fragment(3/5) start size=128MB
[time 00:12.499] kv_cache_flush complete
[time 00:12.622] compute resume
```
Sam: that fragmenting all-reduce looks bad — some microbatches cause 5 fragments, others 1. leads to communication stragglers that break comm/compute overlap.
Jules: hypothesis: uneven KV chunking + per-microbatch kernel selection gives different NCCL kernel paths and different launches -> scatter in op timing.
Anya: agreed. also noticed that when microbatch size is odd (e.g., 3 vs 4 tokens per microbatch), the KV buf packing changes and we hit a fallback memcpy kernel.
Kevin: steps I'm going to try: 1) force KV packing to fixed chunk size 2) add an NCCL fusion window in runtime to coalesce small allreduces 3) pin fused attention kernel for seq_len >= 2048 to avoid fallback.
Sam: quick perf numbers from the baseline run: median lat = 42ms, p99 = 210ms, throughput = 380 t/s. with small fix prototype (KV fixed chunk) we got median 36ms, p99 120ms, throughput 440 t/s.
Anya: nice. can we get a microprofile showing overlap after fusion?
Kevin: attached flame snapshot link: https://internal.srv/flame/1766133330-kvfix (public-ish). shows ~70% overlap after coalescing.
Jules: minor worry: fusion increases memory holding time for gradients. needs safety threshold. propose: only fuse fragments if total fused size < 256MB or latency benefit predicted > 8ms.
Sam: also want runtime opt: prefer kernels that emit single-shot allreduce sizes matching device cap (avoid many tiny reductions). add heuristic in kernel selector: prefer path with stable reduction footprint.
Anya: ran long burn overnight with these knobs. p99 down to 95ms sustained, no regressions in output tokens.
InfraBot: deploy note: rolling canary scheduled at 08:30 UTC. will monitor netcat and perf-alerts.
Kevin: next steps: bake these as config flags (kv_chunk=128MB, allreduce_fusion=enabled, kernel_pref=seq2048_fused) and run regression suite across tensor-parallel layouts.
Jules: also add an eval to catch KV-induced fallbacks: run short prompt set that toggles odd/even microbatch sizes. if any fallback kernels appear, fail.
Sam: good plan. I'll open a follow-up PR with runtime flag names and perf numbers.
Anya: thanks all — this one felt subtle but the KV->comm fragmentation story was real. :party_parrot:
